This Commission vide order dated 23.09.2022 in petition 57/MP/2022, has observed as follows:_ Order in Petition No. 262/TL/2023 3 _Further, we are also of the view that before taking decision regarding the grant of the Transmission Licence to the Petitioner, the comments of the Public may also be invited in light of discussions in Paragraphs 31 and 32 of this Order and that it is being proposed to levy the transmission charges of the said dedicated line on beneficiaries at large. Therefore, we direct that a public notice under clause (a) of sub-section (5) of Section 15 of the Act be published to invite suggestions or objections to the grant of the transmission licence to the Petitioner. The objections or suggestions, if any, be filed by any person before the Commission by 16.08.2024. NRLDC is further directed to furnish the percentage utilization of the KharchamJhakri line month-wise under ISTS using a hybrid methodology as per the 2020 Sharing Regulations._ As per above, before taking a decision regarding the grant of the Transmission Licence to the Petitioner, the Commission directed that a public notice under clause (a) of subsection (5) of Section 15 of the Act be published to invite suggestions or objections to the grant of the transmission licence to the Petitioner. In response to the public notice, no suggestions/objections have been received. 3. The learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that in compliance with the Commission`s direction vide order dated 2.8.2024, NRLDC has filed its affidavit dated 13.8.2024 indicating the percentage utilisation of Karcham- Jhakri line month-wise under ISTS using a hybrid methodology as per the 2020 Sharing Regulations. Learned counsel Order in Petition No. 262/TL/2023 4 added that no suggestions or objections have been received in response to the public notice issued by the Commission under Section 15(5)(a) of the Electricity Act, 2003. The representative of the NRLDC also confirmed the filing of its affidavit in terms of the Commission’s direction vide Order dated 2.8.2024. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the representative of NRLDC, the Commission directed NRLDC to file the following information on an affidavit within two weeks. 5. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that in response to the public notice under Section 15(5)(a) of the Electricity Act, 2003, no suggestion or objection has been received so far. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the representative of NRLDC, the Commission reserved the matter for order. 6.
